A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SK-VQA research. Their complete main texts, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, human evaluations, zero-shot and fine-tuning experiments, filtering ablations, and retrieval-augmented evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds factuality and automated quality assessments, additional model evaluations, and a generation-model comparison.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline retains joint GPT-4 context/QA generation, the same prompt and output parsing, and the same image-reference and answer-presence filters. The LLaVA-34B generation experiment tests an alternative within this pipeline; it does not replace the proposed generator or introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 extends source-specific zero-shot testing beyond the original LAION subset to WIT images with real or generated contexts and COCO-CF images (Tables 6/9). These sources already appeared in dataset construction and training, so this is a limited expansion of tested populations. The external KB-VQA datasets, language and underlying task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 adds LLaVA 13B configurations and evaluates GPT-4o, four Qwen-2.5-VL sizes and six Ovis sizes (Tables 4, 7 and 10), substantially expanding model comparisons. LLaVA-34B also newly participates as an alternative data generator. The original main benchmark comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds 13B fine-tuning and substantial new evaluation protocols: a 50-item factuality audit, grammar checking of 10,000 documents with 50 flagged sentences manually reviewed, and four-dimensional LLM judging. It removes v1's reported 2,853-question hard-subset selection and evaluation protocol. The original standard test sets, metrics and 3B/7B training settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses examine factuality, grammar, bias, toxicity, LLM-assessed quality, source-dependent difficulty, and LLaVA-34B generation failures. Conversely, v1 Appendix A's hard-subset analysis addressing context-only shortcuts disappears. The original filtering ablation and retrieval-augmented experiment remain, although their locations change.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same means and standard deviations across three human annotators. Neither version reports model-run confidence intervals, seed-based uncertainty or significance tests. New audit percentages and cross-model score ranges do not introduce uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Shared benchmark results remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results for 13B fine-tuning, source-specific evaluation and newer models. Examples include GPT-4o's 58.90% and Ovis-34B's 55.20% on SK-VQA, 86% factuality in the human audit, and 76% invalid questions from LLaVA-34B generation. The hard-subset results are removed; these changes are added or removed evaluations, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results, proofs or mathematical derivations. The added quality-scoring rubrics are evaluation protocols, not new theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The central claims about dataset scale, diversity, benchmark difficulty and improved generalization remain. v2 adds an explicit introductory contribution claim that human evaluation affirms the factuality of generated context documents, extending the earlier emphasis on QA quality and training utility.

C2.justification: v2 introduces explanations based on Wikipedia pretraining familiarity and counterfactual distribution shift, interprets narrower Ovis score ranges as benchmark stability, and argues that generation quality requires advanced models. These substantially extend the interpretation and applicability discussion. Some interpretations overreach: Table 9's claimed universal difficulty ordering fails for LLaVA-v1.5-7B, which scores 40.99 on LAION versus 41.40 on COCO-CF.

D1.justification: v1 promises future dataset/code release, whereas v2 supplies dataset and generation-code access links, an important reproducibility addition for this dataset-centered work. v2 also provides quality-check tool identifiers and judge prompts, specifies paragraph-level WIT contexts, and clarifies that existing hyperparameters were not tuned. Conversely, the explicit BEM threshold of 0.5 is no longer documented.

R1.justification: Most related-work discussion remains, but v2 narrows its novelty claim from fully synthetic datasets for training MLLMs generally to adaptation for context-augmented generation. Section 4.6 and Table 11 add positioning through comparisons of synthetic-data quality control, with additional references for newly discussed models and assessment methods.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and introductory contribution summary, reverses the fine-tuning/zero-shot discussion order, promotes retrieval-augmented evaluation into the main text, and moves filtering ablations and limitations into reorganized appendices. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond simply adding experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn from separate example cards into a source-and-generation flow diagram. v2 expands model-result tables, adds source comparisons, quality-control and evaluation-prompt tables, removes the hard-subset table, and relocates Figure 6. The conference layout and single-column appendices also substantially change presentation.

improvement.justification: The new factuality audit, broader model testing and explicit dataset/code links improve empirical assessment and usability beyond v1. The gain is limited by removal of the hard-subset evidence for multimodal necessity and weaknesses in new interpretations, including Table 9's unsupported universal difficulty ordering. Judge independence also remains unclear: Section 4.5 calls GPT-4o a different model, while Appendix H identifies GPT-4o as the generator. Overall, the useful additions support a limited improvement rather than a substantial resolution of validation concerns.
